governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.

rules.text: Keep component code within `src/{model,process,prompts,surfaces,tools,workflow}` and extend existing architecture instead of inventing new concepts.

findings.description: P1 imports every shell export into repository-selected Quality commands while keeping API-key stripping Agent-only, newly exposing shell-only credentials despite describing a toolchain environment.
findings.recommendation: Define, test, and document a Quality-safe shell overlay that preserves PATH and toolchain discovery plus override precedence while excluding direct provider keys and other credential classes.

result.summary: Revise the plan to keep Quality tool discovery without exposing shell-only credentials to repository-selected commands.

checklist.description: Extend the central effective launch-environment policy with a Quality-specific shell projection that overlays only PATH and explicitly vetted non-secret tool-discovery variables between the inherited daemon environment and process-specific overrides, falls back non-disruptively when shell capture fails, and leaves Agent-only credential handling and unrelated process owners unchanged.

Add focused environment-policy and supervised Quality-command regression coverage showing that a synthetic shell-only tool path reaches the executed command, explicit allowed-variable overrides retain precedence, and direct provider keys plus representative non-provider credentials exported by the shell are not imported.

Update the affected process intent documentation to describe Quality's allowlisted host-shell tool-discovery contract, its exclusion of arbitrary exports and credentials, the absence of a hardcoded dotnet path, and the need to restart the daemon after shell configuration changes.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: The revised plan replaces the unrestricted shell import with an allowlist-only Quality projection, adds regression coverage that shell-exported provider and non-provider credentials remain absent while PATH-based tool discovery and override precedence work, and documents that security boundary.

result.summary: Give daemon-launched Quality commands access to shell-configured toolchains through a narrowly allowlisted host-shell overlay so tools such as dotnet are discoverable without exposing shell-only credentials to repository-selected commands.

checklist.description: Extend the central effective launch-environment policy so Quality-owned subprocesses overlay the cached login and interactive shell exports on the daemon environment before process-specific overrides, while keeping direct API-key removal exclusive to Agent processes and treating shell-capture failure as a non-blocking fallback.

Add focused launch-environment and Quality-command regression coverage proving that a tool directory exported only by a synthetic user shell reaches an observed daemon-launched Quality command while explicit overrides and unrelated process-owner behavior remain unchanged.

Update the affected process intent documentation to state that daemon-launched Quality checks use the host shell toolchain environment, that no tool-specific home path is invented, and that shell changes take effect after daemon restart.

result.summary: Make daemon-launched Quality commands inherit the same cached user shell toolchain environment as agent CLIs so shell-configured tools such as dotnet remain discoverable, without hardcoding a tool path or weakening process-specific environment precedence.
